literal: Seven Sons of Daowu, Six Sons of Mingyuan, Five Sons of Taiwu
idiomatic: The Seven Sons of Daowu, the Six Sons of Mingyuan, and the Five Sons of Taiwu

literal: Biographies 4: Seven Sons of Daowu, Six Sons of Mingyuan, Five Sons of Taiwu
idiomatic: Biographies 4 — The Seven Sons of Daowu, the Six Sons of Mingyuan, and the Five Sons of Taiwu

literal: Emperor Daowu had ten sons: the Xuanmu Empress Liu bore Emperor Mingyuan;
idiomatic: Emperor Daowu had ten sons. Empress Liu the Xuanmu bore Emperor Mingyuan;

literal: Consort He bore Prince of Qinghe Shao;
idiomatic: Consort He bore the Prince of Qinghe, Shao;

literal: the Great Consort Wang bore Prince of Yangping Xi;
idiomatic: the Great Consort Wang bore the Prince of Yangping, Xi;

literal: Consort Wang bore Prince of Henan Yao;
idiomatic: Consort Wang bore the Prince of Henan, Yao;

literal: the mothers of Prince of Hejian Xiu and Prince of Changle Chuwén are unknown;
idiomatic: the mothers of the Prince of Hejian, Xiu, and the Prince of Changle, Chuwén, are unrecorded;

literal: Consort Duan bore Prince of Guangping Lian and Prince of Jingzhao Li;
idiomatic: Consort Duan bore the Prince of Guangping, Lian, and the Prince of Jingzhao, Li;

literal: the princes Hun and Cong—their mothers also unknown—all died young and have no biographies.
idiomatic: the princes Hun and Cong—whose mothers are likewise unknown—all died in childhood and have no biographies.

literal: Prince of Qinghe Shao, styled Shouluoba, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Tianxing.
idiomatic: The Prince of Qinghe, Shao, styled Shouluoba, received his fief in the sixth year of Tianxing.

literal: By nature fierce, cruel, and perverse, he delighted in robbing travelers and shooting dogs and pigs for amusement.
idiomatic: Fierce, cruel, and perverse by nature, he delighted in robbing wayfarers and shooting dogs and pigs for sport.

literal: When a pregnant woman came along, Shao cut her open to look at the fetus.
idiomatic: When he encountered a pregnant woman, Shao cut her open to inspect the fetus.

literal: Daowu once grew angry with him and hung him upside down in a well, pulling him out only when he was near death.
idiomatic: Daowu once flew into a rage and hung him head-down in a well, hauling him out only when he was nearly dead.

literal: Mingyuan often rebuked him with moral lessons, and from this they were at odds.
idiomatic: Mingyuan often lectured him on right conduct, and from this the two fell out.

literal: Then Shao's mother Lady He was under censure, and the emperor was about to execute her.
idiomatic: Meanwhile Shao's mother, Lady He, had been condemned, and the emperor was about to put her to death.

literal: Night fell before the decision was made.
idiomatic: Night fell before a decision was reached.

literal: Lady He secretly sent word of urgency to Shao; Shao then, with men of his retinue and several eunuchs, crossed the palace bounds in violation of the ban.
idiomatic: Lady He secretly sent Shao word of her peril; Shao then crossed the palace bounds with men of his retinue and several eunuchs in defiance of the prohibition.

literal: The emperor started up in alarm, could not reach bow or blade in time, and died suddenly.
idiomatic: The emperor started up in alarm but could not reach bow or blade in time, and died on the spot.

literal: The next day the palace gates did not open until noon; Shao claimed an edict summoning the hundred officials to face north before the western palace's Duan Gate, and from between the door panels said: "I have a father, and I also have an elder brother—which of us do you gentlemen wish to follow?
idiomatic: The next day the palace gates stayed shut until noon. Shao claimed an edict summoning the hundred officials to face north before the western palace's Duan Gate, and called from between the door panels: "I have a father, and I have an elder brother—which of us do you gentlemen mean to follow?

literal: " Princes and officials below all turned pale, and none answered.
idiomatic: " Princes and officials alike turned pale; no one answered.

literal: After a long while Duke of Nanping Changsun Song said: "Your servants do not know the circumstances of Your Majesty's passing.
idiomatic: After a long silence Duke of Nanping Changsun Song said: "We do not yet know the circumstances of Your Majesty's passing.

literal: " Only Yinping Xiyuan Lie wept and left.
idiomatic: " Only Yinping Xiyuan Lie wept and withdrew.

literal: Then court and countryside seethed, and every man harbored a different intent.
idiomatic: Court and countryside seethed; every man nursed his own design.

literal: Marquis of Feiru He Hu raised beacon fires north of Anyang city, and all the old Helan clansmen went to join him.
idiomatic: Marquis of Feiru He Hu raised beacon fires north of Anyang, and all the old Helan clansmen rallied to him.

literal: The rest of the former followers likewise led sons and younger kin, summoned old comrades, and gathered here and there.
idiomatic: Other former followers likewise led sons and younger kin, called up old comrades, and gathered in bands across the land.

literal: Hearing that hearts were unsettled, Shao issued cloth and silk in largesse to princes and officials below.
idiomatic: Learning that hearts were unsettled, Shao distributed cloth and silk in largesse among princes and officials.

literal: Earlier, Mingyuan had been away; hearing of the upheaval he returned and hid in the mountains, sending men by night to inform Marquis of Beixin An Tong—and the masses answered him.
idiomatic: Earlier Mingyuan had been away from court. Hearing of the upheaval he returned and hid in the hills, sending men by night to inform Marquis of Beixin An Tong; the masses rallied to him.

literal: Guards seized Shao and delivered him up; Shao and his mother were then granted death, and a dozen eunuchs and palace women who had served as inside accomplices were executed.
idiomatic: Guards seized Shao and delivered him up. Shao and his mother were granted death, and a dozen eunuchs and palace women who had served as inside accomplices were put to death.

literal: Those who had first assaulted the imperial carriage were dismembered alive by the ministers at the capital's southern street and eaten.
idiomatic: Those who had first assaulted the imperial carriage were dismembered alive at the capital's southern street and devoured by the ministers.

literal: Shao was then sixteen.
idiomatic: Shao was sixteen at the time.

literal: Shao's mother was a younger sister of Empress Xianming—beautiful and alluring.
idiomatic: Shao's mother was a younger sister of Empress Xianming, beautiful and alluring.

literal: When Daowu visited the Helan tribe he saw her and was pleased; he told Empress Xianming and asked to take her.
idiomatic: When Daowu visited the Helan tribe he saw her and was smitten; he told Empress Xianming and asked to take her.

literal: The empress said: "You must not.
idiomatic: The empress said: "You must not.

literal: She is too beautiful—ill fortune—and she already has a husband.
idiomatic: She is too beautiful; that bodes ill—and she already has a husband.

literal: " The emperor secretly had her husband killed and took her; she bore Shao, and in the end brought great treason.
idiomatic: " The emperor secretly had her husband killed and took her in. She bore Shao—and in the end brought great treason upon the house.

literal: Prince of Yangping Xi was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Tianxing; clever and accomplished, with refined conduct.
idiomatic: The Prince of Yangping, Xi, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Tianxing. Clever and accomplished, he bore himself with refined conduct.

literal: When Mingyuan drilled troops in the eastern regions he ordered Xi to supervise twelve armies in review; he won great military bearing and received lavish rewards.
idiomatic: When Mingyuan drilled troops in the eastern regions he ordered Xi to supervise twelve armies in review. Xi displayed excellent military bearing and received lavish rewards.

literal: In the sixth year of Taichang he died; the emperor mourned without end.
idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taichang he died, and the emperor mourned without cease.

literal: His eldest son Tuo inherited the title.
idiomatic: His eldest son Tuo inherited the title.

literal: Tuo was honest and generous; in martial arts he had no peer.
idiomatic: Tuo was honest and generous, though in martial skill he had no outstanding peer.

literal: Later his fief was changed to Prince of Huainan; he guarded Wulao and his renown was great.
idiomatic: Later his fief was changed to Prince of Huainan. He guarded Wulao, and his renown was great.

literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen he held the post of Minister of State and was granted a carriage, staff, and table; he need not hurry when entering court.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he served as Minister of State and was granted a carriage, staff, and table; he need not hurry when entering court.

literal: In the twelfth year of Taihe he died.
idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Taihe he died.

literal: Xiaowen was then occupied with the Imperial Ancestor Temple and had just begun the offering; hearing of it he canceled the rite, went in person to mourn with deep grief, and added to the funeral gifts—posthumous title Prince Jing.
idiomatic: Xiaowen was then occupied with the Imperial Ancestor Temple and had just begun the offering. Hearing of Tuo's death he canceled the rite, went in person to mourn with deep grief, and added to the funeral gifts. He was posthumously titled Prince Jing.

literal: His heir Tuwán died early.
idiomatic: His heir Tuwán died young.

literal: His son Prince Xi Xian inherited the grandfather's title and died.
idiomatic: His son Prince Xi Xian inherited the grandfather's title and died.

literal: His son Shizun inherited.
idiomatic: His son Shizun inherited.

literal: Under Emperor Xiaoming he was Governor of Jing Province.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaoming he served as Governor of Jing Province.

literal: On the frontier, generation after generation, raids and counter-raids had been the rule; when Shizun reached the province he forbade harassment.
idiomatic: On the frontier, generation after generation, raids and counter-raids had been the rule. When Shizun reached the province he forbade harassment.

literal: His younger brother Jun was then in Jing Province as commandant of Chaoyang garrison.
idiomatic: His younger brother Jun was then in Jing Province as commandant of Chaoyang garrison.

literal: A southern garrison commandant's wife, on the third day of the third month, was playing along the Mian River; Jun sent his troops to seize her.
idiomatic: A southern garrison commandant's wife, on the third day of the third month, was playing along the Mian River; Jun sent his troops to seize her.

literal: Shizun heard of it, rebuked Jun, and had him transferred back to his original garrison; the Wu people were deeply grateful.
idiomatic: Shizun heard of it, rebuked Jun, and had him transferred back to his original garrison. The Wu people were deeply grateful.

literal: Later he took to bribery and squandered frontier stores, and so his reputation suffered.
idiomatic: Later he took to bribery and squandered frontier stores, and his reputation suffered.

literal: He died as Governor of Ding Province; posthumous title Prince Kang.
idiomatic: He died as Governor of Ding Province and was posthumously titled Prince Kang.

literal: Tuwán's younger brother Zhongkui died early.
idiomatic: Tuwán's younger brother Zhongkui died young.

literal: His eldest son Fashou rose repeatedly to Governor of An Province.
idiomatic: His eldest son Fashou rose repeatedly to Governor of An Province.

literal: Before taking office Fashou sent trusted men in disguise across the border to observe local customs.
idiomatic: Before taking office Fashou sent trusted men in disguise across the border to observe local customs.

literal: On taking his post he at once carried out great rewards and punishments, and the territory became orderly.
idiomatic: On taking his post he at once carried out stern rewards and punishments, and the territory became orderly.

literal: Later he was killed at Heyin.
idiomatic: Later he was killed at Heyin.

literal: His son Qingzhi was greedy and base.
idiomatic: His son Qingzhi was greedy and base.

literal: As chief clerk to the Grand Commandant, on matters great or small he would judge only after receiving something—ten or twenty coins—and take it on the spot; the office called him "Chief Clerk of Ten Coins."
idiomatic: As chief clerk to the Grand Commandant, on matters great or small he would judge only after receiving something—ten or twenty coins—and pocket it on the spot. The office called him "Chief Clerk of Ten Coins."

literal: Fashou's younger brother Faseng held the post of Governor of Yi Province; he killed at will and his wrath knew no constancy.
idiomatic: Fashou's younger brother Faseng served as Governor of Yi Province. He killed at will and his wrath knew no constancy.

literal: Wang, Jia, and other surnames of note within the province—Faseng summoned them all as common soldiers and showed no indulgence.
idiomatic: The Wang, Jia, and other leading families of the province—Faseng summoned them all as common soldiers and showed no indulgence.

literal: Then the whole province rose in revolt and called in outside raiders.
idiomatic: Then the whole province rose in revolt and called in outside raiders.

literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Xu Province.
idiomatic: Later he was appointed Governor of Xu Province.

literal: Faseng had originally attached himself to Yuan Cha; fearing disaster from his arrogance, he plotted rebellion.
idiomatic: Faseng had originally attached himself to Yuan Cha. Fearful that his arrogance would bring disaster upon him, he plotted rebellion.

literal: At the time Director of Documents and concurrently Gentleman-in-Attendance Zhang Wenbo was on mission to Xu Province; Faseng said to him: "I wish to leave danger for safety with you—will you follow me?
idiomatic: At the time Director of Documents and concurrently Gentleman-in-Attendance Zhang Wenbo was on mission to Xu Province. Faseng said to him: "I wish to leave danger for safety with you—will you follow me?

literal: " Wenbo said: "How could I abandon filial duty and righteousness to follow a rebel!
idiomatic: " Wenbo said: "How could I abandon filial duty and righteousness to follow a rebel!

literal: " Faseng was about to kill him; Wenbo cursed: "I would rather die among the cypresses of Wénling than live as a traitor to the state!
idiomatic: " Faseng was about to kill him. Wenbo cursed: "I would rather die among the cypresses of Wénling than live as a traitor to the state!

literal: " Faseng killed him.
idiomatic: " Faseng killed him.

literal: In the first year of Xiaochang Faseng killed the touring commissioner Gao Liang and rebelled at Pengcheng.
idiomatic: In the first year of Xiaochang Faseng killed the touring commissioner Gao Liang and rebelled at Pengcheng.

literal: He styled himself with an honorific title and changed the era name to Tianqi.
idiomatic: He styled himself with an honorific title and changed the era name to Tianqi.

literal: When the great army came to punish him, Faseng fled to Liang.
idiomatic: When the great army came to punish him, Faseng fled to Liang.

literal: More than three thousand military officers garrisoning Pengcheng—Faseng branded their foreheads as slaves and forced them south.
idiomatic: More than three thousand military officers garrisoning Pengcheng—Faseng branded their foreheads as slaves and forced them south.

literal: Emperor Wu of Liang appointed Faseng Minister of Works and enfeoffed him Duke of Shian, later changed to Prince of Song, with great favor.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang appointed Faseng Minister of Works and enfeoffed him Duke of Shian, later changed to Prince of Song, with great favor.

literal: He was further promoted to Grand Commandant and set up as ruler of Wei.
idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grand Commandant and set up as ruler of Wei.

literal: He would not go; he was appointed Commissioner with the Golden Seal, Minister of Works with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, and Governor of Ying Province, then summoned back as Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: He would not go. He was appointed Commissioner with the Golden Seal, Minister of Works with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, and Governor of Ying Province, then summoned back as Grand Commandant.

literal: He died in Liang; posthumous title Prince Xiangli.
idiomatic: He died in Liang and was posthumously titled Prince Xiangli.

literal: His sons Jinglong and Jingzhong.
idiomatic: His sons were Jinglong and Jingzhong.

literal: Prince of Henan Yao was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Tianxing.
idiomatic: The Prince of Henan, Yao, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Tianxing.

literal: At five he once shot a sparrow before Daowu and hit it; the emperor marveled.
idiomatic: At five he once shot a sparrow before Daowu and hit it; the emperor marveled.

literal: When grown, his martial arts were unmatched; with Prince of Yangping Xi and others he directed armies in drill, and all submitted to his courage.
idiomatic: When grown, his martial arts were unmatched. With the Prince of Yangping Xi and others he directed armies in drill, and all submitted to his courage.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His eldest son Ti inherited.
idiomatic: His eldest son Ti inherited.

literal: Fierce and bold with his father's spirit, his fief was changed to Prince of Yingchuan.
idiomatic: Fierce and bold with his father's spirit, his fief was changed to Prince of Yingchuan.

literal: He welcomed the Lady of Brilliant Deportment from beyond the frontier.
idiomatic: He welcomed the Lady of Brilliant Deportment from beyond the frontier.

literal: He was then sixteen, with precocious capacity; the frontier peoples revered him.
idiomatic: He was then sixteen, with precocious capacity; the frontier peoples revered him.

literal: Later his fief was changed to Wuchang; he rose repeatedly to Grand General commanding Tongwan, and was greatly favored.
idiomatic: Later his fief was changed to Wuchang. He rose repeatedly to Grand General commanding Tongwan and was greatly favored.

literal: He died; posthumous title Prince Cheng.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Prince Cheng.

literal: His eldest son He, styled Shanyi, inherited the title.
idiomatic: His eldest son He, styled Shanyi, inherited the title.

literal: At first He betrothed the daughter of Princess Yi's clan as consort and bore a son Xian, but held her in low regard.
idiomatic: At first He betrothed the daughter of Princess Yi's clan as consort and bore a son Xian, but held her in low regard.

literal: Because of the princess he could not send her away.
idiomatic: Because of the princess he could not send her away.

literal: In anger he shaved his head and became a monk.
idiomatic: In anger he shaved his head and became a monk.

literal: Displeased with his mother as well, he abandoned Xian and yielded the title to his next younger brother Jian.
idiomatic: Displeased with his mother as well, he abandoned Xian and yielded the title to his next younger brother Jian.

literal: Jian firmly refused.
idiomatic: Jian firmly refused.

literal: The princess, because her grandson could not inherit, appealed to Xiaowen.
idiomatic: The princess, because her grandson could not inherit, appealed to Xiaowen.

literal: Xiaowen decreed that after Jian's death Xian should inherit; Jian then accepted.
idiomatic: Xiaowen decreed that after Jian's death Xian should inherit; Jian then accepted.

literal: Jian, styled Shaoda, was grave and sparing of words, generous and fond of scholars.
idiomatic: Jian, styled Shaoda, was grave and sparing of words, generous and fond of scholars.

literal: He was Governor of Qi Province.
idiomatic: He served as Governor of Qi Province.

literal: At the beginning of the reforms Jian submitted a memorial following Xiaowen's intent, drawing on Qi customs of old.
idiomatic: At the beginning of the reforms Jian submitted a memorial following Xiaowen's intent, drawing on the old customs of Qi.
